sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

items.prompt: Six boxes hold 8 markers each, and 3 markers are loose. Which expression represents the total?

steps: Six equal groups of 8 are represented by 6 × 8.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A garden has 8 trays with 5 seedlings in each tray and 15 extra seedlings. How many seedlings are there in all?
In 1266, how does the value of the 6 in the ones place compare with the value of the 6 in the tens place?
choices: the same value
10 times as much
1/10 as much
100 times as much

items.prompt: Round each number to the nearest hundred to estimate 3395 - 3023.
Round 964 to the nearest hundred and 43 to the nearest ten, then multiply to estimate the product.
A student says 1019 - 550 = 569. Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is not exact; the exact result is 469 and the rounded estimate is 400.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 469 and the rounded estimate is 500.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 569 and the rounded estimate is 400.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 400.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A student evaluates [68 + 9] × 2 - 13: “They multiply 9 by 2 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 73.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The first error is in the final addition or subtraction; the value should be 142.
The work is correct; 73 is the value.
The student multiplied before evaluating [68 + 9]; the grouped sum is 77, giving 141.
The grouping symbols do not affect the order; 73 is the value.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 211477, the value of the 1 in the thousands place is 10 times as much as the value of the 1 in the ten-thousands place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The values are 1000 and 10000; 1000 is 10 times as much as 10000, so the student's comparison is correct.
The values are 1000 and 10000; 1000 is 1/10 as much as 10000, so the student's comparison is incorrect.
The places are adjacent, so 1000 is 100 times as much as 10000.
The values are 1000 and 10000; 1000 is 10 times as much as 10000.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Which expression means: “Multiply 13 by 2, then subtract the product from 61.”
Which phrase describes 96 - (5 × 9) without evaluating it?
choices: Add 5 and 9, then subtract the sum from 96.
Subtract 5 from 96, then multiply the difference by 9.
Add 96 and 5, then multiply the sum by 9.
Multiply 5 by 9, then subtract the product from 96.
